trust_decision.summary: Whether a namespaced Policy's context entries may read Kubernetes data outside the policy's own namespace is decided per context entry at fetch time: the apiCall urlPath and the ConfigMap namespace are compared against a policy namespace injected through the loader factory, instead of being decided once when the policy is evaluated or admitted.

landing_point.why: The summary names an incomplete cross-namespace read fix, so an engineer looks first at the API read a policy performs: apiCall.Fetch substitutes the urlPath from context and executes it through the raw client with no namespace comparison.

fix_sites.entry_point: API read performed by an engine context entry (kubernetes urlPath through engineapi.RawClient), reached from admission webhook reviews, background/reports scans, cleanup controller and `kubectl kyverno apply`
apiLoader.LoadData, the loader wrapper that builds apicall.New and calls Fetch on the same four engine paths
public API DefaultContextLoaderFactory, used by cmd/kyverno, background-controller, reports-controller, cleanup-controller and cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno
ConfigMap context entry read through engineapi.ConfigmapResolver, reached by the same four engine paths

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The direct executor caller is cluster-scoped GlobalContextEntry controller machinery, and a service-type apiCall is an external HTTP endpoint rather than the Kubernetes urlPath the report names, so neither looks like a namespaced policy's context read.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: ClusterPolicy (empty policy namespace) context entries must keep reading any namespace and any cluster-scoped urlPath, and a namespaced policy's service-type apiCall has an empty urlPath; an over-broad 'namespace segment must equal policy namespace' rule breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: literal urlPath with a namespace segment: /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/... and group form /apis/<group>/<version>/namespaces/<ns>/...
urlPath whose namespace comes from a {{ variable }} that is substituted from context before the check runs
cluster-scoped urlPath with no namespaces segment (e.g. /api/v1/nodes) under a namespaced policy
urlPath containing '..' segments, normalised with path.Clean before matching
empty policy namespace (ClusterPolicy), where the check is skipped entirely
ConfigMap namespace that is literal, substituted from a {{ variable }}, or empty (defaults to the policy namespace for namespaced policies)
non-string substituted ConfigMap name or namespace (e.g. a number), rejected instead of type-asserted

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A namespaced policy's globalReference context entry reads whatever a GlobalContextEntry holds with no namespace comparison, including data selected from other namespaces or from all namespaces
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: GlobalContextEntries are cluster-scoped and created only by a cluster admin, so referencing one is an explicit cluster-level data grant, not a policy-level read.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as one fix site (pkg/engine/context/loaders), different file

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A namespaced policy uses apiCall.service.url pointed at the in-cluster API server; the executor attaches Kyverno's service-account bearer token and performs the request with no namespace check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: service API calls are external HTTP endpoints, not the Kubernetes urlPath path the report and the published check describe.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one file below the apiCall fix site in pkg/engine/apicall

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new context-entry loader for another namespaced resource (e.g. secretRef/resourceRef) copied from configmap.go without a policy-namespace check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: new context entry types in Kyverno are added by copying the existing loader file, so the pre-fix shape propagates with the copy.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second factory option (WithPolicyNamespace) or a new factory caller (the CLI store wrapper) that leaves the namespace empty
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the natural way to plumb the policy identity is a factory option, and every caller of the factory must remember to pass the policy.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a namespaced global-context entry whose watched namespace is forced to the referring policy's namespace
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: GlobalContextEntry already carries a namespace field that defaults to all namespaces, so confining it is a small, natural change.

O9_family: incorrect authorization (CWE-863): namespaced Policy isolation bypassed by context-entry reads
